claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases under conventional solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 follows a multistep crystallization sequence.
A millisecond-scale flash-annealing pulse immediately after rapid quenching will suppress primary-crystal growth.
Suppressing primary-crystal growth by flash annealing will increase amorphous retention.
Flash annealing will improve the thermal stability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The required pre-pulse cooling rate must exceed the minimum cooling-rate boundary for glass formation.
The effective flash-annealing temperature lies above the glass-transition temperature and below the onset of extensive crystallization.
The pulse must occur before nanocrystalline nuclei stabilize during reheating.
The flash pulse temporarily eradicates or re-homogenizes embryonic crystalline nuclei.
A brief temperature spike relaxes internal stresses without allowing enough time for stable crystalline rearrangement.
Flash annealing slightly homogenizes the alloy and melts incipient crystalline regions.
Melting incipient crystalline regions arrests subsequent crystal growth and reduces the development of larger primary phases.
Flash-annealed specimens will have a higher amorphous-phase fraction than rapidly or slowly cooled specimens subjected to conventional reheating.
The higher amorphous fraction will appear in DSC as a smaller or delayed crystallization exotherm.
Flash annealing will increase the crystallization-onset temperature.
Rapid cooling without flash annealing leaves a metastable state containing incipient primary crystallization.
Slower cooling increases crystallization, produces a multiphase microstructure, and lowers amorphous content and thermal stability.

contradictions.description: The pulse is required to remain below sustained-diffusion and extensive-crystallization thresholds, yet the proposed mechanism says that it homogenizes the material and melts incipient crystalline regions. The hypothesis does not explain how a pulse confined between Tg and crystallization onset can melt crystalline regions.
